title: Jensen Huang isn’t out of the woods yet
lede: Russell Brandom argues that Huang's return lifted Nvidia's stock but leaves the company exposed to export-control investigations and to the fallout from Trump's direct intervention.

points: The news sent shares up, especially for neoclouds such as CoreWeave and Nebius, and the Nasdaq rose 7%.
The main open question is how restricted Nvidia chips reached China through Alice Huang's company, and how much Nvidia knew.
The New York Times reported sustained contact between Alice Huang and an officer of China's Ministry of State Security during the affair.
Brandom calls a president phoning a company's board to clear its CEO unprecedented, noting Huang's $25 million gift to Trump's ballroom project.
With Democrats retaking Congress, he expects probes that also reach Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who oversees export controls.

sections.text: The piece argues that with Huang back, any congressional revelation about chips reaching China now damages Nvidia itself, the company much of the AI industry builds on.
